doc_name: Supreme Court of Justice of Bolivia
text: The Supreme Court of Bolivia (Spanish: Corte Suprema de Justicia de Bolivia) served as the country's highest court from 1825 to 2012 and was located in Sucre, 410 kilometres to the south-east of La Paz, Bolivia's capital. It was established by the Supreme Decree (Decreto Supremo) of April 27, 1825, which converted the Royal Audience of Charcas (Audiencia y Cancillería Real de La Plata de los Charcas) of imperial Spain into the Supreme Court of the newly independent Bolivia. The court was officially inaugurated on July 16, 1827. It consisted of 12 ministers (judges) who were elected by the National Congress and served 10-year terms. Manuel María Urcullo was the first President of the Supreme Court of Bolivia, appointed in 1827, and was joined by Ministers Mariano Guzmán, Juan de la Cruz Monje y Ortega, and Casimiro Olañeta. Among the 56 individuals who served as presidents of the court were these and others. The Supreme Court of Bolivia was replaced in January 2012 by the Supreme Court of Justice, as established by the 2009 constitution.
